topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, the scope of the lecture series, and the specific learning outcomes regarding cancer causation and carcinogen appraisal.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: intrinsic mutations, chance, and environmental epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as a genetic and microenvironmental disease and evaluate the relative contributions of endogenous mutations, inherited risks, and environmental factors across global populations.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens and viral oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious agents contribute to malignancy, using the epidemiology, co-factors, and molecular mechanisms of Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific environmental, dietary, and physical agents cause direct and indirect DNA damage through adduct formation, metabolic activation, and oxidative stress.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, including inflammation, promoter signaling pathways in two-stage models, and host developmental susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical, epidemiological, and experimental methods used to link exposures to cancer, ranging from genomic mutational signatures and biobanks to animal and bacterial assays.
